key_insight: A classical optical architecture accelerates quantum-circuit simulation by encoding gates and input-state batches as independent tensor dimensions and supporting eligible tensor-network contractions.
engineering_relevance: Spatial and wavelength multiplexing offer a route to concurrent quantum-simulation workloads without executing each gate–input pair separately.
method: Represent gates and batches of input states as independent tensor dimensions.
Co-design spatial and wavelength encoding and readout for high-order tensor–matrix multiplication in one optical propagation.
Map eligible quantum tensor-network contractions onto the same optical processor.
evidence_signal: Experiments processed all computational-basis inputs for each tested 4-qubit gate; physics-based numerical modeling evaluated Deutsch’s algorithm and all 128 target instances of a 7-qubit Grover algorithm.
watch_item: The algorithm-level results are numerical rather than experimental, so larger-scale hardware accuracy and performance remain to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Quantum circuit simulation with high-order optical tensor processing
